newsitem.title: UK: BBC urges consumer choice in digital era.
newsitem.headline: BBC urges consumer choice in digital era.

text.p: The BBC urged watchdog OFTEL on Wednesday to ensure that genuine consumer choice is maintained when the UK moves into the multi-channel digital television era.

The BBC said that viewers must be able easily to find and select the programmes they want through the Electronic Programme Guide (EPG) which they will use to navigate their way around the sea of up to 200 channels provided by digital services.
They said that viewers should be able to choose whether to receive digital services via satellite, terrestrial or cable distribution without having to buy a different set-top decoder for each system.
"The BBC welcomes OFTEL's role as a tough and proven regulator with a brief to ensure fair competition," said Patricia Hodgson, BBC Director of Policy and Planning.
"Their document asks the right questions. The answers will decide how 22 million households will get television and interactive services in the digital age," she added.
Hodgson was speaking to reporters as the BBC issued its response to draft OFTEL Guidelines to regulate the gateway to digital television and services.
OFTEL has previously been responsible for solely regulating the telecommunications industry.
BSkyB plans to launch digital satellite services offering up to 200 channels into Britain this autumn.

A terrestrial version, which can be received on conventional aerials and will offer around 35 channels, is expected to begin in mid-1998 and cable companies are also likely to upgrade to digital services in the next few years.
A set-top box decoder will be required to receive the programming irrespective of how it is distributed.
Some industry figures have voiced fears that BSkyB will exploit its "first mover" advantage to take a stranglehold on digital broadcasting.
The BBC argued that the EPG should offer viewers simply access to the free-to-air channels by clicking on one button or icon on the front or "home page' display.
It said this page should not be branded with the name of any broadcaster and that the EPG operator should not give its own channels undue prominence.
